question: In 2023, the Commission presented a proposal for a regulation on the establishment of the digital euro1. The ECB aims to be ready for a potential first issuance of the digital euro during 2029, assuming the regulation is adopted in the course of 20262. The Commission presents the digital euro as an equivalent to cash.
At the same time, however, the proposal provides for central data processing mechanisms and imposes limits on digital euro holdings and offline payments.

In an opinion published in 2023, the European Data Protection Supervisor and the European Data Protection Board warned against the excessive centralisation of data, and pointed out that the need to establish an ECB-run fraud detection mechanism had not been sufficiently justified3. The protection of citizens’ privacy calls for specific guarantees rather than mere assurances. 1.
What is the Commission proposing in the way of legal and technical safeguards in order to protect citizens against the use of their digital euro payment data for mass profiling of spending?

Why are the limits on digital euro holdings and offline payments to be based on a decision by the European Commission and the European Central Bank, and not on a regulation adopted by the European Parliament, which is democratically elected, and the European Council, which represents the governments of the Member States?

Will the Commission be in favour of guaranteeing to Poland and other countries outside the euro area a right to restrict or suspend distribution of the digital euro within their territory, in accordance with the allocation of powers at national level, with a view to protecting national monetary policy and financial stability?

European Commission, COM(2023)369 final of 28 June 2023, proposal on the establishment of the digital euro, in particular Articles 16, 32, 35 and 37. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0369. 2 ECB, Communication of 30 October 2025, Eurosystem moving to next phase of digital euro project. https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2025/html/ecb.pr251030~8c5b5beef0.en.html.
